survey: A short wooden pier runs from the beach out into shallow water, seen from the front at three-quarters. Four round wooden posts stand at the corners. The front-left post stands in the sand at the waterline, and the other three stand in the water. The plank deck spans between the posts. It meets the front-left post on the shore, so the pier starts on land and leads out to sea. Short beam ends and support stubs under the front edge and the middle carry the deck down into the water, and the planks are fastened with bolt heads. A handrail runs along each side. The left rail runs from the front-left post to the back-left post and has a short intermediate post. The right rail runs from the back-right post to a short post just behind the front-right post. A coil of rope is wound tightly around the front-left post with no loose ends. A red-and-white life ring hangs on a rope loop from a peg on the front-right post, and it hangs freely below the peg.
